findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes attacker-controlled negative slice to Django
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows start_offset = cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features and offset < 0, then does queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor comes from user-supplied cursor string parsed as value:offset:is_prev, so an attacker can supply a negative offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError/ValueError, causing a 500/DoS. The comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false. If slicing ever succeeded Python semantics would return the tail of the table, bypassing the intended cursor position.

findings.title: Sensitive audit-log endpoint gated to buggy paginator by weak check
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py a user-controlled query param optimized_pagination=true combined with enable_advanced = is_superuser or member.has_global_access routes AuditLogEntry queries to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True. has_global_access is true for many non-admin members, far broader than administrators, so many users can reach the new negative-offset pagination path on a sensitive audit-log dataset. This expands attack surface for DoS and incorrect pagination on security-relevant data.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key logic for datetime ordering
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) assuming a numeric sort key. The audit-log endpoint uses it with order_by='-datetime' where the key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, so building next/prev cursors for any optimized audit-log request crashes instead of paginating.

findings.title: BasePaginator now allows negative slices for prev cursors
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result was changed to start_offset = max(0, offset) if not is_prev else offset. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django does not support negative slicing and raises, so a crafted prev cursor value:negative-offset:1 crashes all BasePaginator users with a 500. For forward cursors it silently clamps invalid negative offsets to 0, returning the first page instead of an error and masking bad cursors.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE corrupts span scores by summing
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the merges use zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) with default AGGREGATE SUM. The Python bulk zadd puts a whole subsegment into the parent key, then the per-span loop unions that parent key into the destination repeatedly, so after the first iteration destination and source overlap on the same payload members. Overlapping members get their end_timestamp_precise scores added (doubled, tripled), corrupting timestamps, breaking zpopmin eviction order so newest/oldest selection is wrong, and polluting scores for later merges. It must use AGGREGATE MAX.

findings.title: Redirect-chain limit cut from 10000 to 1000 fragments deep traces
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the redirect-following loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will stop early with an unresolved set_span_id, leaving spans that belong to one segment in separate Redis sets. Those flush as fragmented segments with wrong segment_id and is_segment flags, causing duplicates and incomplete segments downstream with no metric for truncation.

findings.title: Direct end_timestamp_precise access crashes consumer on old messages
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py process_batch does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with no fallback. Kafka messages buffered before the deploy, produced by older relays, or malformed will lack the field and raise KeyError inside the batch task. That crashes the processing step, stalls commits, causes backlog and repeated retry on a poison message. The field was previously optional for the buffer path, so this is a breaking contract change.

findings.title: Python max-segment-spans guard removed, risks huge segment loads
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py _load_segment_data no longer checks max_segment_spans (1001) and drops oversized segments; it only checks max_segment_bytes. A segment with many tiny spans can be far over the count limit while staying under 10 MiB, causing huge in-memory lists, slow zscan loops, and oversized Kafka produces that can OOM the consumer or downstream. Redis-side zpopmin eviction to 1000 is best-effort and does not cover pre-existing SET keys, races, or other writers, so the Python guard is still needed. max_segment_spans is now dead config.

findings.title: Misleading comment claims negative offsets are safe
findings.body: In src/sentry/utils/cursors.py the Cursor constructor comment says negative offsets are a performance optimization for advanced pagination. Negative offsets are not safe: Django QuerySets reject negative slices and other paginators explicitly raise BadPaginationError for negative offsets. The comment encourages callers to rely on unsafe behavior and contradicts the actual pagination contracts.
